entries.name: Partial Information Decomposition
entries.senseHere: A method that splits the total information two or more sources give about a target into separate pieces: information both sources give redundantly, information each gives uniquely, and information only visible when looking at both sources together.
entries.background: Introduced by Williams and Beer as a way to go beyond simple correlation measures and formally separate overlapping and combined contributions from multiple information sources.

entries.name: Rich club
entries.senseHere: A set of the most highly interconnected neurons in a network, connected to each other far more densely than chance would predict, and found to carry a disproportionate share of both information flow and synergistic computation.

entries.name: Mutual information
entries.senseHere: A number measuring how much knowing one neuron's activity reduces uncertainty about another's, treated here as an undirected, instantaneous statistical dependency rather than a measure of information flow.

entries.name: Transfer entropy
entries.senseHere: A directional measure of how much a source neuron's past activity reduces uncertainty about a target neuron's future activity, beyond what the target's own past already explains. Used in the article as a proxy for information flow between neurons.

entries.name: Functional connectivity
entries.senseHere: A measure of undirected statistical similarity between two neurons' activity patterns, as captured by mutual information, without implying any direction of influence.

entries.name: Effective connectivity
entries.senseHere: A measure of directed, time-ordered influence from one neuron's activity on another's, as captured by transfer entropy, contrasted with the undirected similarity measured by functional connectivity.

entries.name: Synergy
entries.senseHere: Information about a target neuron's activity that is only revealed by looking at two or more source neurons jointly, not disclosed by either source on its own. The article treats it as a signature of genuine neural computation.

entries.name: Redundancy
entries.senseHere: Information about a target that is disclosed equally well by either of two source neurons alone, so it gets double-counted if you simply add up their individual informations.

entries.name: Unique information
entries.senseHere: Information about the target that only one particular source neuron discloses, which no other source could have told you.

entries.name: Redundancy function
entries.senseHere: A formula chosen to measure how much information counts as shared or redundant between source variables; different choices of this formula give different PID results, and no single one is universally agreed upon.

entries.name: Computational triad
entries.senseHere: A basic unit of analysis consisting of two source neurons that both connect to one common target neuron, used as the building block for applying PID across whole recorded networks.

entries.name: Partial information lattice
entries.senseHere: A structured diagram of every possible combination of information sources, ordered so each combination's unique contribution can be calculated by subtracting out what simpler combinations below it already explain.

entries.name: Organotypic culture
entries.senseHere: Living slices of mouse cortex grown outside the body that retain much of the brain's original cell-to-cell connectivity pattern, used here as the source of the neural recordings analyzed with PID.
entries.background: Such cultures let researchers record from hundreds of real neurons over long periods under controlled lab conditions, something far harder to do safely in a live animal.

entries.name: Recurrent connection
entries.senseHere: In a computational triad, a direct link between the two source neurons themselves; more of these was found to increase synergistic integration at the target.

entries.name: Feedforward connection
entries.senseHere: In a computational triad, the links running from the two source neurons to the shared target neuron; both must be present for a triad to count as computational.

entries.name: Feedback connection
entries.senseHere: In a computational triad, a link running from the target neuron back to one of the source neurons; the article found these tend to slightly reduce synergy.

entries.name: O-information
entries.senseHere: A simplified, scalable statistic that approximates whether a group of variables is, overall, more redundant or more synergistic, without computing the full partial information decomposition.

entries.name: Dedekind number
entries.senseHere: A rapidly growing count used here to describe how many distinct information-sharing combinations (PI atoms) exist for a given number of source neurons, explaining why PID becomes computationally intractable for many sources.

entries.name: Local PID
entries.senseHere: A version of PID applied to single specific moments or configurations of activity rather than averaged over all possible states, producing a time-resolved trace of redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy over time.

entries.name: Integrated information decomposition
entries.senseHere: An extension of PID that decomposes shared information between multiple sources and multiple targets at once, rather than just multiple sources feeding a single target, enabling analysis of how information flows over time between whole systems.

entries.name: Möbius inversion
entries.senseHere: A calculation method used on the partial information lattice that finds the information uniquely contributed by a combination of sources by subtracting away everything already accounted for by simpler combinations below it.
